contentHtml:
Bengaluru: The Karnataka Government has constituted a six member Special Investigation Team (SIT) to investigate an alleged interstate network involved in the unlicensed repacking and relabelling of spurious and expired medicines worth more than Rs 4.91 crore. The development follows the seizure of a large quantity of medicines from an unlicensed facility operating from a farmhouse near Bidadi in Bengaluru South district.

The alleged racket came to light during an inspection conducted by the Karnataka Food Safety and Drug Administration (FSDA) on August 18, 2026, at a farmhouse in Bidadi. Officials seized medicines, expired stock, counterfeit labels, packaging material and an injection filling unit, with the total value of the recovered material estimated at ₹4.91 crore. The operation allegedly involved obtaining lower cost medicines and repacking and relabelling them to make them appear to be products of reputed multinational pharmaceutical companies.

The seized medicines reportedly included products carrying the names of major pharmaceutical companies, including Pfizer. The labels on the recovered medicines allegedly contained non functional QR codes and barcodes, raising concerns about the authenticity and traceability of the products. The suspected operation is being investigated for allegedly introducing repackaged and relabelled medicines into the pharmaceutical supply chain.

The seizure included 5,640 vials of CEFIAVIGENT 2.5 Injection, valued at approximately ₹3.38 crore, and 1,531 vials of HIZLAM Injection, valued at around ₹52.24 lakh. Officials also recovered expired medicines worth approximately ₹35 lakh.

Another major recovery comprised 470 vials of Xavitaz Injection, valued at around ₹27.49 lakh, and 264 vials of EMBLAVEO, valued at approximately ₹20.59 lakh. The EMBLAVEO labels carried the name of Pfizer Limited.

The seized stock also included 165 vials of Zavicefta Injection, valued at about ₹5.45 lakh, and 44 vials of TIGYNT IV, valued at approximately ₹2.06 lakh. The TIGYNT IV labels carried the name of Stanex Drugs and Chemicals.

Officials further seized 44 vials of Tigvnet Injection, valued at around ₹2.06 lakh, 190 vials of Aztreo Injection worth approximately ₹1.48 lakh, and 50 vials of Trezam Injection valued at around ₹1 lakh.

The preliminary investigation has indicated that medicines were allegedly sourced from Himachal Pradesh, Telangana and other States, suggesting possible interstate links to the operation. Karnataka authorities have therefore decided to investigate the broader network involved in sourcing, repacking, relabelling and distributing the suspected spurious medicines.

The authorities have also arrested Prabhudev Gowda, a worker allegedly associated with the facility. The investigation will examine his alleged role as well as the identities and activities of other individuals who may have been involved in the operation.

The six member SIT will be headed by Joint Commissioner of Police C Vamshikrishna. The team has been constituted following the August 18 inspection and seizure and will investigate the alleged unlicensed repacking and relabelling activities and their possible interstate connections.

The SIT has also been declared a police station under the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023. It will function under the supervision of the Additional Director General of Police, Law and Order. The team has been authorised to submit police reports before the competent courts and is required to provide periodic progress reports to the State Government.

The formation of the SIT comes amid concerns that the suspected spurious medicines may have entered the wider healthcare supply chain. Officials are examining the source of the medicines, the manner in which they were allegedly repacked and relabelled, and the network through which the products may have been distributed. The investigation will also seek to establish whether hospitals, pharmacies or other buyers received the suspected counterfeit products, reports The New Indian Express.
